literal: Non-lying, non-lying if practiced, other virtues not doing, not doing is good.
translation: If one consistently practices the virtue of truthfulness without fail, then even if one does not perform any other virtues, it is still good.
modern: பொய்யாமை என்னும் அறத்தை ஒருவன் தொடர்ந்து கடைப்பிடித்தால், அவன் வேறு எந்த அறங்களையும் செய்யாமல் இருப்பதுவே அவனுக்கு நன்மையைத் தரும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme status of truthfulness, defined here as the avoidance of falsehood. By repeating the words 'பொய்யாமை' (non-lying) and 'செய்யாமை' (not doing), the poet uses emphasis to show that truthfulness alone is sufficient for a virtuous life. If a person can strictly adhere to speaking the truth under all circumstances, they do not need to perform other moral or ritualistic deeds. The simple act of avoiding falsehood is so powerful that it encompasses and surpasses all other virtues.
